record.paper_title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials
record.context_brief: Possible failure of the Vanishing Conjecture for non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent series
record.original_question: Does there exist a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails? Equivalently, can one find a non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C for which Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) does not vanish for all sufficiently large m, or prove that no such example exists?

evidence.quote: One interesting question is whether or not the VC fails (as the JC does) for any HN formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] but P (z) not in C[z]? To our best knowledge, no such counterexample has been known yet.
Open Problem 5.2. Find a HN formal power series P (z) in C[[z]] but P (z) not in C[z], if there are any, such that the VC fails for P (z).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}[[z]]=\mathbb{C}[[z_1,\dots,z_n]]$ denote the ring of formal power series in $n$ variables over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^n \partial^2/\partial z_i^2$ denote the Laplace operator. A formal power series $P(z)\in\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ is called Hessian nilpotent (HN) if its Hessian matrix $\mathrm{Hess}(P)=(\partial^2 P/\partial z_i\partial z_j)$ is nilpotent as a matrix over $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$. The Vanishing Conjecture (VC) for $P(z)$ asserts that
$$\Delta^m\!\bigl(P(z)^{m+1}\bigr)=0\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }m\ge 1.$$

Determine whether there exists a Hessian nilpotent formal power series $P(z)\in\mathbb{C}[[z]]\setminus\mathbb{C}[z]$ (i.e., not a polynomial) for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails — that is, $\Delta^m(P^{m+1})\ne 0$ for infinitely many $m$ — or, alternatively, prove that no such non-polynomial counterexample exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search shows the Vanishing Conjecture for Hessian nilpotent series is an active reduction of the Jacobian Conjecture, and no counterexample (polynomial or non-polynomial) appears in the available sources. The problem of finding a non-polynomial HN formal power series violating the VC, or proving none exists, does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: A Vanishing Conjecture on Differential Operators with Constant Coefficients
status_evidence.snippet: The Jacobian conjecture has been reduced to a vanishing conjecture on Laplace operators and Hessian nilpotent polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The VC is studied as a reduction of the Jacobian Conjecture; sources discuss formulations but no non-polynomial counterexample is reported.

status_evidence.title: Two results on homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Results on homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomials in the context of the vanishing conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Research focuses on polynomial cases; the non-polynomial formal power series case remains unaddressed in available references.
